subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state become a generic top-level persisted message contract, or remain inside an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope such as `__openclaw.inboundDecoration`?
rationale: Both representations can solve the bug, but they establish materially different long-term ownership and compatibility boundaries for serialized messages; code review cannot safely select the permanent public/internal contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope
options.body: Move the marker and bare body under one named `__openclaw` decoration slot, then prove writer/readers preserve and clear it correctly.

options.title: Approve the top-level contract explicitly
options.body: Keep the top-level fields, document them as a supported serialized contract, and add compatibility proof for transcript and consumer round-trips.

options.title: Pause and consolidate direction
options.body: Hold this branch until the linked issue and related implementation proposals establish one shared contract owner.

recommendation.title: Use an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope
recommendation.body: Move the marker and bare body under one named `__openclaw` decoration slot, then prove writer/readers preserve and clear it correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidenced non-branch contributor in the supplied history who implemented and documented the alternative metadata-owner boundary.
